A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed from StreamMultiDiffusion to SemanticDraw. The text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO mask-IoU results, throughput ablations, and qualitative regional and panorama generation experiments, including appendix results.

after.justification: v3 reports original FID, Inception Score, CLIP, and timing results across several diffusion configurations in Tables 1–6, alongside retained generation demonstrations.

M1.justification: v1 Algorithm 2 and v3 Algorithm S2 retain the same noise-after-aggregation procedure, white-background mask-centering bootstrapping, and quantized masks. Multi-prompt stream batching and the optional Tiny AutoEncoder also remain. The additional backbone evaluations do not establish a changed generative algorithm.

E1.justification: Coverage remains COCO-based regional generation, arbitrary-size panorama synthesis, and drawing/editing demonstrations with optional background images. The nine-prompt large-scene example already appears in v1. Additional backbones and samplers change experimental configurations within these retained tasks.

E2.justification: The retained Irworobongdo comparison gains MD+LCM in v3 Figure 2, reporting 4m 47s; v1 Figure 11 compares only MultiDiffusion and the proposed method. MultiDiffusion remains the comparator family throughout the expanded model/sampler evaluations; newly discussed methods such as SpaText are not benchmarked.

E3.justification: v3 replaces the segmentation-IoU evaluation with FID, Inception Score, and separately specified foreground/background CLIP scores. Beyond v1's SD1.5/LCM experiments, it evaluates Hyper-SD, SDXL with Lightning/Euler Discrete, and SD3 with Flash FlowMatch, using model-specific 512×512 or 1024×1024 configurations.

E4.justification: The same cumulative stabilization ablation changes from spatial IoU evidence in v1 Table 1 to perceptual-quality and prompt-adherence evidence in v3 Table 5. The throughput ablation and mask-blur sensitivity examples are retained. The large-scene case additionally demonstrates failure of naive LCM acceleration.

E5.justification: v1 Table 1 reports IoU values with ± terms, whereas v3's replacement evaluations report point estimates only. Neither PDF explains those earlier ± terms or specifies repeated-run counts, so this establishes removal of uncertainty reporting without establishing fewer experimental runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds four quality/speed comparison tables and replaces the IoU ablation scores with FID/CLIP results. For example, Table 1 reports SD1.5/LCM FID 270.55 for MultiDiffusion and 93.93 for SemanticDraw, without a same-metric v1 counterpart. The original throughput sequence ending at 1.57 FPS and the 52.5× large-scene speedup remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v3 removes the explicit forward-noising definition and algebraic clean-image estimator from v1 Section 3.1, Equations 1–2. The aggregation, denoising/noise-separation, and quantized-mask mathematics remain equivalent. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 makes compatibility with any existing diffusion model and acceleration scheduler a central abstract/conclusion claim, broadening v1's focus on LCM-compatible MultiDiffusion. The semantic-painting contribution remains. The newly emphasized approximately 50× speedup comes from the already reported large-scene example.

C2.justification: v3 Section S1.3 adds an uncertainty and rough-sketch interpretation of progressively expanding masks. It drops v1 Section 5.2's explicit discussion of remaining sampling cost and imperfect mask fitting, and the LCM-induced color-style qualification. Mask-alpha sensitivity and the autoencoder quality/speed tradeoff remain discussed.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents the COCO validation split, prompt construction, nearest-neighbor mask resizing, and the three-prompt-pair throughput setting. Appendix S3.2 specifies supported backbone/accelerator combinations and updates application instructions. Conversely, v1's 0.3 alpha preprocessing for occluded masks in the large-scene example is omitted.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recast around acceleration, a control-method taxonomy, and generation from multiple regional prompts. Added discussions include SpaText, GLIGEN, InstanceDiffusion, Hyper-SD, Flash Diffusion, and flow matching. This broadens positioning beyond the earlier LCM/MultiDiffusion integration and extensive editing/inpainting discussion.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and related-work narrative are extensively rewritten around SemanticDraw. Method preliminaries are condensed, experimental exposition is reorganized, panorama discussion moves into the supplement, and new supplement subsections expand streaming-execution and mask-quantization explanations.

P2.justification: The paper changes from single-column to two-column presentation with extensive display reorganization. v3 merges the bootstrapping and architecture diagrams, relocates and annotates the execution schedule, expands and restructures numerical tables, consolidates panorama panels, and replaces application screenshots. The large-scene figure moves into the introduction with an added comparator panel.

improvement.justification: Broader model/sampler validation and clearer experimental documentation are substantial gains. However, v3 removes the quantitative spatial-mask-fidelity evidence and explicit limitations, while its new Tables 1 and 5 report final-method FID 93.93 versus 78.21 despite describing the same setup, without reconciliation. These competing changes in evidential breadth and reliability prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
